security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, ordinary financial prose, or safe argument-array subprocess use. Confirmed risks include unquoted symbol placeholders, a predictable user-derived temporary path, stale cached responses, and an external MCP trust boundary; no prompt injection or credential-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: User-supplied symbols can alter the temporary output path.
remediation.suggestion: Validate symbols against supported ticker syntax and create each run with tempfile.mkdtemp inside a controlled directory.

remediation.issue: Failed refreshes can leave older JSON files active.
remediation.suggestion: Use a new directory per run or remove each prior JSON file before fetching, then bind all outputs to one run identifier.

remediation.issue: Shell examples place SYMBOL or RAW_DIR placeholders into executable commands without safe quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Pass values as argument arrays where possible. Otherwise validate values, quote them for the active shell, and avoid embedding paths in Python source.

remediation.issue: The pre-earnings workflow writes to a fixed shared temporary filename.
remediation.suggestion: Replace /tmp/data.json with a securely created unique file and ensure the file is removed after parsing.

remediation.issue: The MCP fallback adds a remote service to the agent environment.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and describe the endpoint, transmitted query data, authentication scope, and removal procedure before configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Symbol Controls Output Path
semantic_findings.description: The command-line symbol is inserted into a temporary directory name after only replacing periods. Slash and parent-directory segments can redirect fixed JSON and error files outside the intended directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow from sys.argv to the Path expression is direct, and no allowlist or path containment check is present.

semantic_findings.title: Failed Refresh Can Reuse Stale Financial Data
semantic_findings.description: A failed fetch writes an error file but leaves any older JSON file intact. The reporting path prefers JSON over errors, so a new analysis can silently use stale results.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The output directory is stable per symbol, failure does not remove prior JSON, and section reads JSON before checking the current error file.

content.user_title: Analyze Earnings Before and After Results
content.value_statement: Earnings data is fragmented across statements, estimates, calls, and market feeds. This skill organizes those inputs into timely previews, summaries, and valuation reports.
actual_capabilities: Determines whether a request needs a pre-earnings preview or post-earnings analysis.
Collects Longbridge statements, consensus, ratings, segments, news, quotes, and price history in parallel.
Creates concise post-earnings cards covering surprises, trends, segments, thesis changes, expectations, and risks.
Compares prior management guidance with actual performance for upcoming earnings preparation.
Builds Markdown research reports with DCF, trading-comparable, and relevant precedent-transaction valuation.
Responds in English, Simplified Chinese, or Traditional Chinese based on the user's language.
limitations: Requires the Longbridge CLI, a configured Longbridge MCP connection, or supplemental public web data.
Transcript, whisper-number, and options-implied-move coverage depends on available web search results.
Source data can be delayed, incomplete, stale, or inconsistent across reporting periods.
Outputs are research aids, not personalized investment advice or guaranteed forecasts.

use_cases.title: Prepare for an Upcoming Release
use_cases.description: Review prior guidance, recent events, consensus gaps, management credibility, and key questions before results.

use_cases.title: Summarize Reported Results
use_cases.description: Turn quarterly data into a concise beat-or-miss card with segment, margin, outlook, and risk analysis.

use_cases.title: Update a Valuation View
use_cases.description: Create a sourced research report with revised estimates, scenario valuation, target price, and rating rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Earnings Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the latest reported earnings for [SYMBOL]. Show major beats or misses, guidance changes, segment trends, and key risks.

prompt_templates.title: Upcoming Earnings Preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a pre-earnings preview for [SYMBOL]. Compare prior guidance with actual performance and identify three to five questions for this release.

prompt_templates.title: Detailed Results Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [SYMBOL] for [QUARTER]. Explain KPI surprises, margin drivers, segment performance, management guidance, estimate revisions, thesis changes, and market expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Full Valuation Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full Markdown earnings report for [SYMBOL]. Include sourced estimates, DCF, peer multiples, relevant transactions, scenarios, target price, rating, and risks.

output: Revenue beat consensus while net margin improved from the prior year.
Gaming and advertising led growth, while fintech remained stable.
Next-quarter expectations imply slower growth, with regulation and spending as key risks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a pre-earnings preview for TSLA.US.
output: Prior delivery guidance remains the main performance benchmark.
Consensus and management assumptions diverge most on automotive margins.
Watch pricing, factory utilization, energy growth, and updated capital spending.

output_examples.input: Create a full earnings report for a global retailer.
output_examples.output: The report presents KPI variances, estimate revisions, three valuation scenarios, a weighted target price, rating rationale, risks, and dated source links.

best_practices: Specify the ticker, exchange, reporting quarter, and whether results are upcoming or released.
Verify every source covers the same fiscal period before comparing results or estimates.
Treat ratings and target prices as research inputs, then apply independent judgment.
anti_patterns: Do not request precise conclusions when the ticker or reporting period is ambiguous.
Do not treat current consensus as the historical estimate baseline without checking its date.
Do not use generated ratings or price targets as automatic trading instructions.

faq.question: Which markets does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It supports United States, Hong Kong, and mainland China shares when Longbridge data is available.

faq.question: Can it analyze results before they are released?
faq.answer: Yes. Pre-earnings mode reviews prior guidance, recent events, consensus gaps, call themes, and key questions.

faq.question: What is the default post-earnings output?
faq.answer: The default is a concise in-chat card covering KPIs, segments, trends, thesis status, expectations, and risks.

faq.question: Can it create a full research report?
faq.answer: Yes. An explicit request produces a Markdown report with detailed analysis, valuation scenarios, target price, rating, and sources.

faq.question: Does it require Longbridge access?
faq.answer: Longbridge CLI or MCP access provides the intended data. Public web search can supplement missing transcripts and selected market context.

faq.question: Does the output constitute investment advice?
faq.answer: No. The output supports research and may contain errors or uncertain assumptions. Verify source data and use independent judgment.
